title: Persistence library source
description: The sources name a shipped persistence library but do not supply it. The stack declares persistence.md and sqlite.md, so the DATABASE step copies the shipped Rigging library unchanged and generates the schema package from DATABASE.md.
system_choice: Copy the shipped Rigging persistence library through the DATABASE step. No other story writes persistence code.

title: Phase sequencing
description: ANALYSIS.md gives ten sequencing groups. Phases follow those groups so that no depends edge points to a later phase.
system_choice: Phase equals the ANALYSIS.md sequencing group. Foundations are phase 1 and the terminal grader is phase 10.

title: CLI skeleton split from dispatch
description: The CLI platform contract publishes main() and cli_runner, while CLI-001 owns usage-error routing. Both could be one story or two.
system_choice: Split them. cli-foundation supplies the package, main(), cli_runner, and the launcher. cli-dispatch adds routing and exit 2 handling.

title: Location of the recorded architecture sections
description: The Blueprint copy under blueprint/ is a protected Drydock artifact, so I wrote the Technology Stack and Module Ownership sections to ARCHITECTURE.md at the build root instead. Is that acceptable, or should it live elsewhere on replan?
system_choice: The Blueprint copy under blueprint/ is a protected Drydock artifact, so I wrote the Technology Stack and Module Ownership sections to ARCHITECTURE.md at the build root instead. Is that acceptable, or should it live elsewhere on replan?

title: Lint scope for Drydock-generated persistence/
description: The generated persistence/schema.py annotates rows with VARCHAR(n)/INTEGER, which are undefined names, and the shipped postgres.py/testing.py fail ruff. I excluded persistence/ from ruff in pyproject.toml (extend-exclude) rather than editing generated or shipped code. Is that acceptable, or should the generator emit lint-clean output?
system_choice: The generated persistence/schema.py annotates rows with VARCHAR(n)/INTEGER, which are undefined names, and the shipped postgres.py/testing.py fail ruff. I excluded persistence/ from ruff in pyproject.toml (extend-exclude) rather than editing generated or shipped code. Is that acceptable, or should the generator emit lint-clean output?

title: main() on argparse exits
description: main catches the SystemExit argparse raises for usage errors and --help and returns its code, so main never exits in-process. The launcher and python -m cli still exit with that code.
system_choice: main catches the SystemExit argparse raises for usage errors and --help and returns its code, so main never exits in-process. The launcher and python -m cli still exit with that code.

title: Placeholder command dispatch
description: commands.dispatch returns 2 with an unknown-command diagnostic for every command, because no handlers exist until cli-dispatch. This is intentional and will be replaced by routing.

title: Empty DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_PATH
description: Treated an empty value as unset and fell through to the next source, matching run.sh's ${DATABASE_URL:-...} behavior. Is that acceptable, or should an empty value be used literally?

title: Indexes derived from the persistence declaration
description: The rendered schema indexes transactions(account); transactions(category). Each is implied by the declaration — a foreign key is looked up by its child column, and a read pattern's Input fields are the predicate it filters on. Declare an `- INDEX (...)` bullet in DATABASE.md for any index this does not cover.
